newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka unlikely to impose more limits on grid power.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka unlikely to impose more limits on grid power.

text.p: Sri Lanka's state power utility is unlikely to impose more limits on the use of grid power as water levels in depleted hydroreservoirs have held steady with the onset of intermonsoon showers, officials said on Friday.

The Ceylon Electricity Board (CEB) plans to double thermal power generation capacity by June with the addition of new permanent diesel power plants to the grid and the purchase of electricity from private plants, they said.
"We now have 241 gigawatt hours, about 19 percent of our storage, in the hydropower reservoirs, roughly the same level as at the start of April," a CEB official said.
"It seems that this time we'll have no problems except for the restrictions already imposed to conserve electricty," he said.
The government recently banned the use of air-conditioners operating on power from the national grid and urged private sector businesses to use their own generators.

The restrictions were imposed after water levels in hydroreservoirs, which supply 85 percent of grid power, plunged to dangerously low levels with the failure of the northeast monsoon and the delayed onset of intermonsoon showers.
The Indian Ocean island has two rainy seasons. The southwest monsoon, the most important for fuelling hydroelectric plants, usually starts around the third week of May.
A Meteorology Department official said the southwest monsoon is expected to break by the end of May.

"Until then we'll get evening thunder showers, although not every day," deputy director P. M. Jayatilaka Banda told Reuters. "We expect the monsoon by the third week of May or by the end of May. It is still too early to say exactly when."

The CEB has said it plans to cut dependence on hydropower to 57 percent of the requirement by building more thermal power plants by June 1997. The island now has an installed capacity of 1,135 megawatts of hydropower and 250 megawatts of thermal power.
